drafts.subject: Quick critique on an agent-ops control idea?
drafts.body: I am pressure-testing a short service for teams about to give AI agents real tool permissions. The idea is not compliance certification: it is a practical review of which agent actions need approval, what evidence should be kept, and what happens when outcomes drift. Would this solve a real worry for a founder/operator, or does it sound like process theater?
drafts.clear_feedback_question: What part would feel urgent enough to spend time on before scaling an agent workflow?

drafts.style: AI agent builder technical critique request
drafts.subject: Critique request: agent workflow control review
drafts.body: I am testing a no-software-first offer for agent teams: map tool-call permissions, human approval points, trace/evidence requirements, and rollback/escalation before workflows get real permissions. It does not claim compliance or production readiness. From a builder view, is this a missing preflight step or would existing tracing/eval tools already cover it?
drafts.clear_feedback_question: Where would this break down for a real agent builder?

drafts.subject: Request for critique on AI-agent operations review concept
drafts.body: I am preparing a concept for an Agent Ops Control Review: a short diagnostic for teams moving agent workflows from demo to real business operations. It maps action boundaries, owner approvals, audit evidence, and residual risks. It is explicitly not legal compliance, certification, or a live platform. Would this be a credible early productized service, or is the wedge still too abstract?
drafts.clear_feedback_question: What would you need to see before recommending this to a founder or AI team?
